title: Arena Hard Auto - LLM Pairwise Evaluation
description: Pairwise evaluation of LLM responses on challenging prompts from the Arena Hard benchmark (Li et al., ICML 2025). Annotators compare two responses on a continuous scale and rate question difficulty.
overview: Arena-Hard-Auto is a benchmark of 500 challenging, open-ended prompts for evaluating chat models. It was created by Tianle Li and colleagues at UC Berkeley (the LMSYS / LMArena group) using the BenchBuilder pipeline, and published at ICML 2025. It was built to separate strong models more cleanly than earlier automatic benchmarks while staying aligned with human preferences.

The prompts were mined automatically from large crowd-sourced conversation datasets, Chatbot Arena and WildChat-1M, by selecting for difficulty and quality. In the original benchmark two model responses to each prompt are compared by an LLM-as-judge. The annotation task here is the human version of that judgment: read the prompt and both responses, then say which is better and by how much.

Arena-Hard-Auto reports 98.6% correlation with human preference rankings and about three times the model separation of MT-Bench, at a cost of roughly $20 per evaluation run. The prompts cover open-ended tasks rather than fixed multiple-choice questions, which is what makes graded pairwise judgment the natural annotation format.

The Potato config below reproduces this comparison with a pairwise scheme on a -3 to +3 scale (A much better through Tie to B much better) and a five-point Likert scale for prompt difficulty. Use it to collect graded human preference judgments on model outputs, for example to validate an LLM-as-judge setup or to build preference data.
